Description: UNESCO site; first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. Citations: Glenn D. Lowry (1987), 'Humayun's Tomb: Form, Function, and Meaning in Early Mughal Architecture'; Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'.

Monumental entrance to the courtyard that housed Persian craftsmen for Humayun's Tomb. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; AKTC Report (2010), 'Humayun's Tomb Urban Renewal Project'.
Located inside Humayun's Tomb complex; octagonal tomb on raised platform. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
Decorated marble and sandstone tomb in Nizamuddin built for Akbar's prime minister. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

Built for his wife and later his own resting place; stripped for Safdarjung's Tomb. Citations: Allison Busch (2011), 'Poetry of Kings: The Classical Hindi Literature of Mughal India'; AKTC Conservation Document (2020).

Imperial palace fortress of red sandstone forming Shahjahanabad's core. Citations: Ebba Koch (2001), 'The Complete Taj Mahal and the Riverfront Gardens of Agra/Delhi'; Gordon Sanderson (1914), 'The Red Fort, Delhi: Archaeological Survey of India Memoir'.

One of India's largest congregational mosques, built with red sandstone and white marble. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Stephe Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'.
Vast Mughal garden surrounding the open-air pavilion tomb of Princess Roshanara. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.

Royal country palace and garden where Aurangzeb crowned himself emperor in 1658. Citations: Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.
Small three-domed private mosque built entirely in white marble inside Red Fort. Citations: Ebba Koch (2002), 'Mughal Architecture'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.

Unique hall constructed entirely of white marble with 64 pillars in Nizamuddin. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
11-arched stone bridge spanning the Kushak Nallah near Nizamuddin. Citations: Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.
Small tomb in Nizamuddin decorated with Persian glazed tilework (chini). Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
Historic traveler resting house on GT Road, later site of 1857 battle. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.
